clue.text: In perpetuity putting an end to children's stories

definitions.meaning: lasting without end, for all time

definitions.text: putting an end to children's stories
definitions.meaning: the closing formula of fairy tales, where the couple live happily on endlessly

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: the second half is the traditional tag that ends bedtime stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eternally, and it is also the stock closing words of a fairy tale.

clue.text: Flighty young woman says: "Father swallows bad apple"

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into its middle, as if eating it

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of apple are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a priest choking on a rotten apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says' looks like a homophone signal but is only a link. 'bad' makes LAPPE, and 'swallows' sets it inside the priest's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapper was a fashionable, carefree young woman of the 1920s, the type called flighty.

clue.text: King bound to be reformed

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
bound together as partners, so allied

explanation.surface: A monarch is tied by duty to be made better.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops that have reformed have regrouped and come together again, which is what rallied means.

clue.text: Five with malaria become faint

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ague is an old name for malarial fever

explanation.surface: Five patients catch malaria and pass out.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint as an adjective means indistinct or hazy, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Leftist attack? You can stuff it!

parts.note: a red is a left-wing radical
to pepper is to bombard, as with shot or questions

explanation.surface: A left-winger's assault is rudely dismissed by the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can stuff it!' reads as a rude brush-off but is a literal definition: peppers are commonly stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell peppers are a classic vegetable for stuffing with rice or meat.

clue.text: See 1
Weep with mother when these reading desks turn up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the joined letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sob is to weep
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A child cries with its mother when church lecterns appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses SOBMA as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambos, plural of ambo, are the raised pulpits or reading desks of early churches.

clue.text: Loose little girl longed to embrace university head

parts.note: deb, short for debutante, is a young society girl

indicators.note: one piece hugs the other inside it

parts.note: ached means yearned or longed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small girl yearned to hug the head of her college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little girl' is a deb, not a diminutive; 'head' gives U, which 'to embrace' sets inside the word for longed, making AUCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose in the old moral sense means dissolute, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Prisoner found in wretched cluster of houses

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting inside another

parts.note: vile means wretched or base
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A convict is discovered in a miserable housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small group of houses in the country, a cluster smaller than a town.

clue.text: Bacon's more headstrong son

parts.note: rasher is the comparative of rash, impetuous
s is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon's boy is described as even more reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like the philosopher, but it is the breakfast meat; 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers are thin slices of bacon, so bacon here is a plural collection of them.

clue.text: One escorted round stage as suspected

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: one piece goes around another

parts.note: led means guided or escorted
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Someone was guided around a theatre platform, as people suspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged describes something claimed or suspected but not yet proved.

clue.text: Murmurs from two bishops opening packages

indicators.note: the two letters open up the other word and sit inside it

parts.note: bales are bound bundles of goods
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two make BB

explanation.surface: Two clergymen mutter while unwrapping parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: To babble is to murmur, as a brook babbles with a low continuous sound.

clue.text: Funny figure getting smaller

definitions.meaning: hilarious, extremely amusing in informal use
read as two words, a cost becoming lower

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: the second sense splits the answer into PRICE and LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the answer means hilarious; split in two it suggests a cost reducing.

clue.text: Treatment makes us decline

parts.note: to age is to decline with years

explanation.surface: How we are handled causes us to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means the way something is handled or treated, as in rough usage.

clue.text: Broadcaster wants a day in Rio

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the city name

explanation.surface: A radio host wants a day's holiday in Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a device or station that broadcasts sound.

clue.text: These solid figures heard Cato, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: The Roman statesman Cato may have heard about some geometric solids.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solids with eight faces, a family of geometric figures.

clue.text: Handouts demonstrating speed obtained in breaking plates

indicators.note: one piece is found lodged inside another
breaking smashes the plates into a new order

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: Leaflets show how fast someone got while smashing crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' makes PALETS; 'obtained in' sets the speed unit inside it, and 'demonstrating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamphlets are leaflets handed out to the public, so handouts is a synonym.

clue.text: Mean chap would made an intermediary

parts.note: a mean is an average or middle value
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A stingy fellow would act as a go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy but is the average sense; 'would made' is a misprint for 'would make', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman is a go-between who acts between two parties, especially in trade.

clue.text: Nearly see red about female relation having rambled

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the relation
nearly means the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: an aunt is a female relative
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone almost lost their temper over an aunt who had been wandering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' trims only the first word, leaving SE, so with the colour the outer piece is SERED; 'about' wraps it around the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauntered means strolled in a leisurely way, so rambled is a close synonym.

clue.text: Boosts volunteers

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition, both senses verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both increases and comes forward to offer oneself.

clue.text: For pa, getting in and out becomes impractical

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters gathered turn into something new

explanation.surface: Father's coming and going is getting unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges the pooled letters of PA, IN and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian schemes are idealistic and unrealistic, so impractical fits.

clue.text: Imagine Dr West coming back!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the name returns, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: Picture a doctor called West returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to imagine or fantasise.

clue.text: End of mobile rental, complicated and indestructible

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
complicated tangles the letters of rental

explanation.surface: Ending a phone rental is complicated and seems to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' gives E from mobile; 'complicated' rearranges RENTAL into TERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, so it cannot be destroyed.

clue.text: Fellows with fading remains of past emotions, having married

parts.note: embers figuratively are the dying traces of a passion

explanation.surface: Society fellows with cooling old feelings have got married.
explanation.definitionFit: Members, like fellows, belong to a society or college.

clue.text: Male (skilled) married, returning to church

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a married couple are made one
ch is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A skilled man got married on his way back to church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a man's name glossed by its meaning: the Hebrew name is usually taken to mean trained or skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch is a Biblical male name, traditionally said to mean dedicated or skilled.

clue.text: Reserved flower to make face ointment

parts.note: cold means distant, aloof or reserved
the flower of something is its best part, its cream

explanation.surface: A shy bloom is used to make a facial lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts as a river or bloom; it is the finest part, as in the flower of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is an emollient cleansing cream applied to the face.

clue.text: One hundred, no spring chicken, so cooped up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
idiom for someone no longer young

explanation.surface: A centenarian, far from young, is confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Caged means shut up in a cage, like hens cooped up.

clue.text: Smart girl with copper chain

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tie is a link or chain binding things

explanation.surface: A chic young woman wears a copper necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, smart-looking girl.

clue.text: Poke behind part of leg in lively do

indicators.note: the poke comes after the leg part

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
a dig is a poke or jab

explanation.surface: Someone jabs a shin at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy, lively party, informally called a do.

clue.text: Eat mine all cut up: what a performance!

indicators.note: cut up means chopped into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A diner tells someone to finish their chopped food, complaining of the fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all cut up' rearranges EAT MINE. 'what a performance!' sounds like exasperation but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance at a theatre.

clue.text: The seamstress's sensation?

parts.note: a tingling numbness, cheekily credited to someone who works with sewing tools

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the prickling feeling of a limb waking up, and a seamstress handles such sharp tools.

clue.text: See 27
